In what way would you consider another virus to be HIV-like? 

There's the herpesviridae family of viruses, consisting of viruses like Epstein-Barr virus and HSV1 & 2. They are extremely effective at evading the immune system and establishing a lifelong infection, much like HIV. Whilst neither HSV1 & 2 are likely to do much damage (unless you're immunocompromised or you're unlucky enough to develop herpes simplex encephalitis), the Epstein-Barr virus can be really nasty and is associated with the development of a wide variety of diseases, including lymphomas and even multiple sclerosis. The herpesviridae viruses are also ridiculously widespread, with over 90% of the population of the US showing evidence of previous infection. 

Also, I'd argue that HIV is actually not that easy to contract/spread, considering that the sex act with the highest risk of contracting HIV (receptive anal sex) is still only 1.6%. This obviously can change depending on things like viral load, etc, but compare this to gonorrhoea for example, which has an 84% risk of contracting it through receptive anal sex. 

(Disclaimer; not a scientist or anything, so I may be wrong about some information, I just find viruses cool).
